title: Family story v1 (authored source: content/families/<slug>.json)
description: FINAL contract (story v2 fields are optional additions: reference/story/story-v2.md). Authored by humans and agents; everything generated (voice clips, poses, timeline, track) lives in <slug>.voice.json and <slug>.bake.json, never here. Only the JSON Schema keywords listed in STORY-BIBLE section 12 are used, so a zero-dependency checker can enforce this file. Rules a schema cannot say (word counts, dashes, banned phrases, app and anchor existence, disclosures, cross-field and cross-family rules) are enforced by scripts/validate-stories.mts. Enumerations are mirrored as constants in assets/story/types.ts and a test keeps the two equal.

slug.description: Public URL slug (/family/<slug>), from the fictional surname(s). Must equal the casting.json slug for this house. Never derived from the house id.

house.description: INTERNAL HouseSpec id (content/houses/<id>.json). Build-time only. It never appears in a URL, a file name, a title, an og tag, alt text or any displayed string.

notes.description: Build-only notes for reviewers and the owner (for example 'beat X needs owner sign-off'). Never shipped, never displayed.

appId.description: A Companion Hub store id from content/story/catalog-apps.json (r-catalog: live store AND manifest on main). Unknown ids fail.

voiceKey.description: Key of content/story/voices.json. Never an engine voice name.

category.description: The beat's topic. The landing page topic chips are these minus 'setup'. home = household logistics (planner, inventory, paperwork); iot = devices on the home network; media = photos, music, film, books; kids = children's learning and play; small-business = running a business or self-employed work.

surname.description: Fictional surname, one or two parts. Shown as 'The <surname> family'.

tagline.description: One sentence, sentence case, no dashes, ends with a full stop, no price, no guarantee. Shown on the card and in the share title.

business.description: True when someone in the household runs a business or is self-employed from home. Drives the small-business beat quota.

story.description: Two to three short sentences that open the family page. Third person. Who they are and what they do. Never a testimonial: no quote, no 'says', no result claim.

line.description: House number and an INVENTED street, for example '14 Larkfield Lane'. No ZIP, no postal code, no region.

place.description: An INVENTED town or neighbourhood. Not a real place. Unique across the fleet.

day.description: Optional (story v2). A day in the house: 5 to 10 entries in time order, each pointing at an existing beat. Each adult or teen member appears at least once (warning otherwise).

home.description: Optional (story v2). The house, told true to its spec. No builder, no game, no real place, no address, no numbers: the page derives storeys, area and room count itself.

lede.description: At most 50 words (validator counts) in two or three sentences, each at most 22 words. True to the house spec: storeys, materials, rooms, garden, light. No fireplace, TV, crib or island the house lacks; no house name or id.

room.description: An exact room name of the house (the validator checks it against the spec).

line.description: At most 16 words (validator counts), true to that room's furniture.

at.description: Part of the day, daylight only. Entries run in this order and never go back.

beat.description: An existing beat id of this file.

line.description: At most 14 words (validator counts); a different sentence from the beat's own title and body.

detail.description: Optional (story v2). What a visitor who stays opens up: how it worked with the service it replaces, how it works now, the steps, one true fact. The popup's title and body (the narration, the film, the ads) are not touched.

before.description: At most 28 words (validator counts). How it works with the service it replaces: neutral and factual. Names a service only if it is in the beat's app.replaces or the catalog entry's replaces; never an attack on a company.

after.description: At most 28 words. What the person does now and where it lives (the mechanism), not an adjective.

steps.description: What the person actually does, in order; each at most 12 words. No UI described as seen on a screen.

fact.description: At most 28 words. One true fact about the app in the words of its catalog description (the validator warns when it shares no word with it).

bio.description: At most 45 words (validator counts). Who they are and how they use the Core: third person, present tense, no age (the page shows it), no health, legal or financial claim.

name.description: The name the member gave their agent. A story device, not a product setting. Unique across the fleet.

runtime.description: Hermes = messaging gateway (text it); OpenClaw = browser automation and tool use. First-party store ids ci-hermes and ci-openclaw.

job.description: One sentence naming tasks the listed apps can really do. Third person, present tense.

personality.description: Three plain words. They colour the caption tone, never a capability.

voice.description: The agent's voice for beat.say lines. Different from the narrator and from every other companion in the family.

memory.description: True when this member has connected Companion Memory (beta) to the agent, opt-in. If any member has it, the first mention of Companion Memory in the file reads 'Companion Memory (beta)'.

limits.description: What it will not do alone, for example 'Drafts only. Dad sends every message.'

work.description: Occupation or school, a short noun phrase: 'bakery owner', 'secondary-school teacher', 'second grade'. Not a medical, legal or financial qualification claim.

colour.description: CI-Common chart token for the monogram disc. Distinct within a family where possible. Never a hex.

archetype.description: Optional. The job this member does on the family's one Companion Core (reference/story/personas.md, content/story/personas.json): organiser, builder, gamer, learner, maker, host, tech-family, business-owner, creative, contractor, marketer, lawyer, journalist, educator, money-keeper, housemate, carer, community-lead, researcher, seller, translator, archivist, traveller, athlete, collector or shift-worker. A member with an archetype needs a beat in one of its rooms and a beat whose app is in its pool; a family with archetypes covers at least two. Members without one are not held to the persona rules.

companion.description: Optional. At least one member has one; at most three do. Members under 16 never have one (rule age-companion); babies, children and visitors never do.

room.description: Required for kind room and outside.

title.description: Sentence case. 'The kitchen', 'Out in the garden'.

room.description: Narrow to this room when the house has several instances.

nth.description: Which instance, in the resolver's stable order.

fallback.description: Tried in order when the role is missing in this house. Required for every role that is not in roles.json universal. The validator FAILS when neither the role nor a fallback resolves in the beat's house.

camera.description: Semantic hints only. The pose solver still picks a collision-free eye with a clear sight line.

side.description: Which third of the frame the anchor sits on; the popup takes the other.

kind.description: 'phone' draws a stylised phone with the `phone` rows. Never a screenshot, never an SSID, a password or a pairing code.

title.description: At most 6 words (validator counts). Sentence case. A complete thought, not a label.

body.description: At most 30 words (validator counts), each sentence at most 20 words, no digits except inside an app name. THIS TEXT IS THE NARRATION: the voice tool reads it word for word and the caption shows it. Third person, present tense.

chips.description: The app name, then (story v3) 'alternative to <Service>' for a beat that has `service`: exactly two items, the second naming the registry service (content/story/services.json) or the alias app.replaces[0] uses. The pass 1 form 'replaces <X>' (X one of the app's catalog `replaces` names) is accepted with a warning (chips-legacy). Nothing else.

note.description: A required disclosure line for this beat, see STORY-BIBLE section 8 (ftue-pick carries 'Installing apps uses the internet.').

speaker.description: A member id whose companion speaks. Must have a companion.

text.description: At most 16 words, first person, one or two short sentences. SCRIPTED: no claim about what the agent is or knows, no product fact, no number. Shown in the popup as a quote labelled 'Scripted'. At most 6 beats per family have one.

member.description: Whose life this beat is about. Omit for household beats (FTUE, outro).

agent.description: A member id whose companion acts in this beat. Requires `approval`.

approval.description: The member who reads, decides or sends. Every beat with an `agent` has one: an agent prepares, a person approves.

replaces.description: A subset of the catalog `replaces` of this app (empty for first-party apps and for apps that replace nothing).

with.description: Other store apps named in this beat's text. Every Hub app named in a beat must be `app.id` or listed here. Companion Memory, Hermes and OpenClaw are exempt (the first-party trio).

capability.description: The ONE thing the app does in this scene, in the words of its catalog description. Build-only audit trail (never shipped). The validator warns when it shares no word with the app's catalog description.

service.description: Optional (story v3). The id of the replaced service this beat's app is the alternative to, from content/story/services.json. At most one. Present exactly when app.replaces is not empty; app.replaces[0] is then the service's name or one of its aliases. A family with at least one beat that has `service` is a v3 family: the v3 rules (age-chat, age-companion, app-avoid, service-missing, household-beats, household-doer, persona-band, pair-share, pair-budget, chips-legacy) are errors there and warnings in every other family (scripts/story/lib/v3.mts isV3Story). reference/story/story-v3.md.

wake.description: FTUE plug-in beat only: the Core's LED, fan and screen wake.

film.description: In the film (see STORY-BIBLE section 7 for the film quota).

minSeconds.description: Reading floor. The beat lasts max(voice + 0.6 s, popup read time, minSeconds).

body.description: At most 30 words. Second person to the viewer. Names Companion Core and one concrete thing the family now does at home. The sign-off 'UnCloud your life.' and the beta line are added by the site and the film from claims.json; never type them here.
